summary: Encoder input is NOT an RGB image. Each obs frame is a 224x224x3 uint8 image packed as (ch0 = normalised INVERSE depth v=(1/Z-1/Z_far)/(1/Z_near-1/Z_far), Z_near 0.20 m / Z_far 3.00 m, near=1, far/invalid=0; ch1 = validity mask 255 where depth_mm>0; ch2 = exact copy of ch0), built by umi_handheld/build_dp_depth_zarr.py:284-296 and reproduced bit-for-bit at deploy by rov_gui/perception/policy_obs.py:643-662. The dataset divides by 255 (umi_dataset.py:286) and the image normalizer is identity scale 1/offset 0 (normalize_util.py:39-51), so the timm backbone sees float32 in [0,1] with NO mean/std normalisation anywhere (encoder transforms = RandomCrop(212)->Resize(224,bilinear,antialias)->RandomRotation(+-5, fill 0), ColorJitter removed; deploy = CenterCrop(212)->Resize(224)). CLIP-B expects mean/std (0.481,0.458,0.408)/(0.269,0.261,0.276); DINOv3 expects ImageNet (0.485,0.456,0.406)/(0.229,0.224,0.225); neither is applied, and the actual per-channel stats of the training obs (400-frame uniform subsample of /home/bdml/Desktop/data collection/dataset_depth.zarr.zip, this session) are ch0/ch2 mean 0.276 std 0.159, ch1 mean 1.0000 std 0.005 (validity is ~constant 1: 99.94 % of frames >=0.985 valid per rov_gui/tools/dp_policy_out/training_validity_20260902.txt). Effective information content is a single greyscale-like inverse-depth plane in R and B plus a near-constant G plane, median metric range 0.62 m, 4.3 % of valid pixels clipped to 0 at >=3 m. Land demos: OAK-D-W in air, FoundationStereo depth on the alpha=0 rectified-left grid (fx 249.566 px @640x400) is re-projected with a pure ray-to-ray remap (no extrinsics, INTER_NEAREST) onto the C3's RAW CAM_B underwater projection from the EEPROM (fx 757.12 @1280x800 scaled to 640x400, 85.6 deg HFOV), then centre-cropped 400x400 (x0=120) and nearest-resized to 224; the 0.64 depth scale in the plan doc is NOT applied on this path (depth_scale_applied 1.0). 224 was inherited from upstream UMI (task shape [3,224,224], vit_base_patch16_clip_224 is fixed-size) — no independent justification found. Moving to 256 for DINOv3 is config-plus-rebuild: --out-res 256 (dataset rebuild from the existing depth/ stores), task yaml shape, and deploy obs_res in config/hw_mpc.yaml:691 / backends/policy.py:143; the encoder crop/resize, projection (1024->768 Linear), and denoiser cond-token count all follow automatically, and DINOv3 (RoPE, dynamic_img_size) runs at 224 (201 tokens) or 256 (261 tokens) while the current CLIP-B asserts at 256.

risks_for_dinov3: Input statistics mismatch: DINOv3 was pretrained on ImageNet-normalised RGB (mean ~0.45, std ~0.23 per channel, after Normalize roughly zero-mean unit-var); the encoder here receives raw [0,1] with ch0/ch2 mean 0.276 std 0.159 and ch1 a near-constant 1.0 plane (std 0.005). Without adding a Normalize, the patch-embed sees inputs ~2 std off the pretraining distribution in G and compressed in R/B. Adding Normalize is a code change in transformer_obs_encoder.py (currently none) and must be mirrored in rov_gui/perception/dp_policy.py:650-661 for parity. [유도 from measured stats + timm cfg]

Semantic mismatch: the 'image' is a duplicated inverse-depth plane in R and B with a constant G — a magenta-tinted greyscale relief, not a natural photo. DINOv3's RGB patch-embed and low-level features carry no prior for this encoding; the large-model advantage (LVD-1689M self-supervised RGB features) is largely lost on the first layer, and the plan doc itself notes 'depth 입력에 CLIP ViT 사전학습 이득 거의 없음' (DP_TRAJECTORY_PLAN.ko.md:155-156). A greyscale-replicated 3-channel (ch0,ch0,ch0) packing would be closer to what RGB pretraining tolerates, but that changes the data contract and the validity channel would need another home. [유도]

Validity channel is uninformative in training (99.94 % of frames >= 0.985 valid, per-pixel mean 1.0000) but can differ underwater (rect_left border zeros when coverage < 1, stereo dropouts on turbid/textureless scenes, RandomRotation corners are the only zeros the training set sees). A high-capacity encoder can latch onto ch1 as a spurious constant; any deployment-time ch1 structure is OOD. [유도 from training_validity_20260902.txt + policy_obs.py:80-93]

Range clipping: 4.3 % of valid pixels are clipped to 0 at >= 3 m and are indistinguishable in ch0 from invalid; median range 0.62 m, so most of the [0,1] code space (v>0.74 => Z<0.26 m) is nearly unused. DINOv3 fine-tuning does not fix this encoding limitation. [측정 this session, dataset_depth.zarr.zip subsample]

Train-time augmentation is per-minibatch (one crop, one angle for all 128 images, transformer_obs_encoder.py:277-278) and the crop->Resize is bilinear on inverse depth + mask; with a much larger encoder and only ~12.6k training windows from 75 episodes, over-fitting pressure rises and the effective augmentation diversity is lower than it looks.

Resolution/tokens: DINOv3 timm cfg is 256 (fixed_input_size flag True, but RoPE + dynamic_img_size make 224 legal: 201 tokens). Training at 224 keeps the current dataset; training at 256 needs a dataset rebuild (--out-res 256), task yaml shape, and deploy obs_res edits in config/hw_mpc.yaml:691 + backends/policy.py:143 — and the deploy coverage threshold 0.985 was derived on the 224 grid. Cond tokens per frame rise 197->201 (224) or 261 (256); the denoiser sizes itself automatically. The 4 register tokens are forwarded to the denoiser as conditioning (feature_aggregation null) — harmless but not meaningful. [유도]

Env split: training env umi2 (timm 0.9.7) has no dinov3 registrations; deploy env rovgui-pose (timm 1.0.29) does. A DINOv3 checkpoint trained after upgrading timm in umi2 must still load strict in rovgui-pose (dp_policy.py builds the encoder with pretrained=False and strict-loads state dict, :666-680); timm version skew between train/deploy is a new parity surface for dp_policy_parity.py. [유도]

Compute/memory on one RTX 5090 32 GB [예측]: full fine-tuning (frozen False, EMA on) of ViT-L (303 M) ≈ 1.2 GB weights + grads + 2×Adam + EMA ≈ 6 GB plus activations for 128 images × 24 layers × 201 tokens — feasible, probably with bf16/grad-checkpointing; H+ (840 M) ≈ 17 GB before activations — marginal; 7B (6.7 G params) cannot be fine-tuned (27 GB fp32 weights alone) and even frozen fp16 (13.4 GB) competes at deploy with FoundationStereo (~46 ms, memory measured elsewhere) and the 8-step DDIM loop on the same GPU; the station's intake budget already stalls at 7.26 Hz FS (rov_gui/backends/policy.py:46,83). Frozen-encoder use also changes the contract (`frozen: True` asserts pretrained, transformer_obs_encoder.py:99-102) and forfeits adaptation to the depth encoding.
License: timm tags DINOv3 weights 'dinov3-license' (Meta DINOv3 license), unlike CLIP-B 'apache-2.0'; check terms before shipping a checkpoint. [스펙: timm pretrained cfg]

Does the plan's ResNet/CLIP-vs-DINOv3 expectation ('depth 입력에 사전학습 이득 거의 없음') still hold? The only existing ablation (dp-ablation-groupnorm-wins) compares ResNet34 BN/GN vs CLIP ViT-B; there is no depth-specific pretrained-encoder result to extrapolate from.

The rectified-C3 target model is still unavailable (EEPROM has no stereo extrinsics, target_camera_underwater.yaml:60-70), so training frames are on the RAW CAM_B grid while live depth arrives on rect_left and is inverse-rectified with a per-pixel z correction (policy_obs.py:44-70); this residual grid mismatch is independent of the encoder choice but bounds what any encoder can fix.
